items.title: Bob Lovett Interview, 1949-04-01
items.q: Franz Jackson invited him to play when Bob Schaffner was ill.

ctx.x: Well, I would like... I think sometimes that I would like to play and you pick up the clarinet and your fingers don't move as fast as they used to and your lip gets tired and so you get discouraged and you put it away and you don't touch it again for a long time. And so every time you pick it up it works, so eventually you just stop altogether. Too fresh, isn't it? Yes, yeah. That's one of those things you have to keep at it constantly or else you lose touch with it.

Well, so many people who drop out of music find an opportunity to play once in a while and decide that they, oh, we'll forget the loss of technique forgetfulness of tunes and so forth. Yeah. Well, you just go ahead and try. Yeah. And I know that they feel somewhat disappointed with their performance. Yeah. Others are so disappointed and I think that maybe they were a little tense in their original endeavors. that they were so devoted that they can't stand that disappointment. George Mitchell is one of those. Oh.…
Right. Yeah, it is a distressing thing.
